files.lesson.md: --- order: 13 unit: solving node: AC9M8A02 n2 uses: [AC9M8A01 n1] # expanding brackets first assumes: [AC9M8A02 n1] # graphing lines: Linear relations (Lines and their rules); the Run board draws both lines, so plotting is not needed here title: Solving harder equations summary: "Get the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other, doing the same to both sides; expand any brackets first. Then check by substituting into the first equation." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Two phone plans: 7 dollars plus 3 a gigabyte, or 5 a gigabyte minus a 9 dollar credit. When do they cost the same? 3x + 7 = 5x − 9." connection: plans-cross # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8175 url: http://127.0.0.1:8175/index.html readySelector: "#legend" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: graph.yml#explain, caption: "$y = 3x + 7$ and $y = 5x - 9$ meet at $(8, 31)$: both sides of $3x + 7 = 5x - 9$ equal 31 when $x = 8$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@graph.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Same to both sides, then check" say: "Collect the x terms on one side, the numbers on the other." clip: - caption: { text: "3x + 7 = 5x − 9. Take 3x from both sides: 7 = 2x − 9.", say: "Take three x from both sides. Seven equals two x take nine." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Add 9 to both sides: 16 = 2x. Halve: x = 8.", say: "Add nine to both sides, then halve. x is eight." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "Check: 3 × 8 + 7 = 31 and 5 × 8 − 9 = 31. The lines meet at x = 8.", say: "Check: both sides are thirty one. The lines meet there." } - wait: 1600 --- In Year 7 you solved equations with the balance method, even with $x$ on both sides. Year 8 equations add negatives, brackets and fractions, where blocks on a scale no longer help. The rule is the same: **do the same to both sides**, until $x$ is on its own. Then **check**: put your answer back into the first equation. If both sides are equal, it is right. ## Predict: when do they cost the same? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a solution of 3x + 7 = 5x − 9 before solving shows whether they can reason about both sides; the graph then shows the solution as where the two sides are equal." check: type: predict q: "Which value of $x$ makes $3x + 7 = 5x - 9$ true?" options: - "$x = 8$" - "$x = 1$" - "$x = -8$" - "$x = 2$" actual: "x = 8. Check: 3 × 8 + 7 = 31 and 5 × 8 − 9 = 31. Both sides are equal." ``` Try each option in both sides. Or solve it: what could you take from both sides first? ## Run: where both sides are equal ```step stage: run insight: "Each side of the equation is a line; the solution is where they meet, because there both sides have the same value." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "The two lines are $y = 3x + 7$ and $y = 5x - 9$. Drag $P$ to where they meet. Was your prediction right?", when: "P on y = 3x + 7 and P on y = 5x - 9" } ``` Read $P$'s coordinates. Which number is the solution, and what does the other one tell you? ## Investigate: same to both sides ```step stage: investigate insight: "Move the smaller x term (so the x term stays positive), then the numbers, then divide; substitute to check. Ben's mistake takes 7 away to undo − 7, instead of adding it." tasks: - check: type: working q: "Solve $3x + 7 = 5x - 9$. Write one step per line." start: "3x + 7 = 5x - 9" form: subject x example: ["7 = 2x - 9", "16 = 2x", "x = 8"] wrong: [["8x + 7 = -9", "8x = -16", "x = -2"], ["7 = 2x - 9", "-2 = 2x", "x = -1"]] explain: "Take 3x from both sides: 7 = 2x − 9. Add 9: 16 = 2x. Halve: x = 8." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ben" text: "Ben solves $2x + 5 = 4x - 7$. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: inverse-sign explain: "Line 3: to undo − 7, add 7 to both sides: 12 = 2x, so x = 6. Check: 2 × 6 + 5 = 17 and 4 × 6 − 7 = 17." - check: type: answer q: "Check $x = 8$ in $3x + 7 = 5x - 9$: what is the value of each side?" answer: "31" feedback: - ["8", "That is x. Put 8 in for x on each side."] explain: "3 × 8 + 7 = 31 and 5 × 8 − 9 = 31: equal, so x = 8 is right." ``` ### Solve, then check Here is how to solve with $x$ on both sides. ```worked 3x + 7 = 5x - 9 :: $x$ is on both sides. 7 = 2x - 9 :: Take $3x$ from both sides (the smaller $x$ term, so $2x$ stays positive). 16 = 2x :: Add 9 to both sides: this undoes $- 9$. x = 8 :: Divide both sides by 2. 3(8) + 7 = 31,\; 5(8) - 9 = 31 :: Check in the first equation: both sides are 31. ``` Now solve it yourself, one step per line. The checker marks the first line that does not follow. ### Find the mistake Read Ben's working one line at a time. How do you undo $- 7$? ### Check by substituting ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a bracket, a negative answer, a fraction, brackets on both sides, then the edge case of an equation with no solution." tasks: - check: type: working q: "A bracket: solve $2(x + 3) = x + 10$. Expand first. One step per line." start: "2(x + 3) = x + 10" form: subject x example: ["2x + 6 = x + 10", "x + 6 = 10", "x = 4"] wrong: [["2x + 3 = x + 10", "x + 3 = 10", "x = 7"]] explain: "Expand: 2x + 6 = x + 10. Take x: x + 6 = 10. Take 6: x = 4. Check: 2(4 + 3) = 14 and 4 + 10 = 14." - check: type: answer q: "A negative answer: solve $4x - 3 = 7x + 12$." answer: "-5" feedback: - ["5", "Check it: 4 × 5 − 3 = 17 but 7 × 5 + 12 = 47. Watch the signs."] - ["3", "Take 4x from both sides first: −3 = 3x + 12."] explain: "Take 4x: −3 = 3x + 12. Take 12: −15 = 3x. So x = −5. Check: 4(−5) − 3 = −23 and 7(−5) + 12 = −23." - check: type: answer q: "A fraction: solve $\\dfrac{x}{3} + 2 = 6$." answer: "12" feedback: - ["4", "That is x/3. Multiply by 3 to undo ÷ 3."] - ["24", "Take 2 away first: x/3 = 4."] explain: "Take 2: x/3 = 4. Multiply by 3: x = 12. Check: 12 ÷ 3 + 2 = 6." - check: type: working q: "Brackets on both sides: solve $3(x - 2) = 2(x + 1)$. One step per line." start: "3(x - 2) = 2(x + 1)" form: subject x example: ["3x - 6 = 2x + 2", "x - 6 = 2", "x = 8"] wrong: [["3x - 2 = 2x + 1", "x = 3"]] explain: "Expand both: 3x − 6 = 2x + 2. Take 2x: x − 6 = 2. Add 6: x = 8. Check: 3(6) = 18 and 2(9) = 18." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: solve $2x + 3 = 2x + 5$. What happens?" options: ["No value works: taking 2x away leaves 3 = 5, which is never true", "x = 1", "x = 0"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Check: 2 + 3 = 5 but 2 + 5 = 7.", "Check: 3 is not 5."] explain: "Taking 2x from both sides leaves 3 = 5: false for every x, so there is no solution. On a graph, the two lines are parallel and never meet." ``` ### A bracket Each task changes one thing. Check each answer by substituting. ### A negative answer ### A fraction ### Brackets on both sides ### No solution ## Practise: solve and check ```step stage: practise insight: "Equations with x on both sides, negatives and a geometry context, mixed; the inverse-sign slip is planted again; the review keeps expanding fresh." tasks: - check: type: working q: "Solve $5x - 4 = 2x + 11$. One step per line." start: "5x - 4 = 2x + 11" form: subject x example: ["3x - 4 = 11", "3x = 15", "x = 5"] wrong: [["3x - 4 = 11", "3x = 7", "x = 7/3"]] explain: "Take 2x: 3x − 4 = 11. Add 4: 3x = 15. x = 5. Check: 21 = 21." - check: type: answer q: "Solve $6 - x = 2x - 9$." answer: "5" feedback: - ["-5", "Check: 6 − (−5) = 11, but 2(−5) − 9 = −19."] - ["1", "Add x to both sides first: 6 = 3x − 9."] explain: "Add x: 6 = 3x − 9. Add 9: 15 = 3x. x = 5. Check: 1 = 1." smaller: check: { type: "answer", q: "Add $x$ to both sides. What does the right side become?", answer: "3x - 9", explain: "$2x + x = 3x$, so the right side is $3x - 9$ and the left side is just 6." } - check: type: answer q: "Angles on a straight line are $3x$ and $x + 20$ degrees. Find $x$." answer: "40" feedback: - ["45", "3x + x + 20 = 180, so 4x = 160."] - ["160", "That is 4x. Divide by 4."] explain: "3x + x + 20 = 180, so 4x = 160 and x = 40. The angles are 120° and 60°." - check: type: answer q: "Review: expand $4(2x - 3)$." answer: "8x - 12" form: expanded feedback: - ["8x - 3", "The 4 multiplies the 3 as well."] explain: "4 × 2x = 8x and 4 × (−3) = −12." ``` ### x on both sides ### Negative x ### Angles ### Review: expanding ## Make: build an equation ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a second line that meets y = 2x + 1 at x = 3 builds an equation with that solution, reversing the lesson: from the answer to the equation." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["At x = 3, the first line is at y = 7. Your line must pass through (3, 7).", "Try m = 4: then c must make 4 × 3 + c = 7."] check: { type: board, text: "Set $m$ and $c$ so that $2x + 1 = mx + c$ has the solution $x = 3$, with $m$ more than 2.", when: "3m + c = 7 and m > 2", explain: "For example m = 4, c = −5: 2x + 1 = 4x − 5 gives x = 3. Any line through (3, 7) works." } ``` Write your equation, then solve it on paper to check. ## Make: when do two plans match, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Two price lists are two expressions; setting them equal and doing the same to both sides finds the usage where they cost the same, and substituting into both bills is the check." hint: ["Write each bill with x for the gigabytes, then set them equal.", "Take the smaller x term, 4x, from both sides first."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Plan A costs 10 dollars a month plus 4 dollars per gigabyte. Plan B costs 7 dollars per gigabyte, with a 5 dollar credit taken off the bill (made up for the task). At how many gigabytes do the two plans cost the same?" steps: - ["Let $x$ be the gigabytes. Plan A: $4x + 10$. Plan B: $7x - 5$", "write each bill in terms of $x$"] - ["$4x + 10 = 7x - 5$", "the bills are equal"] - ["$10 = 3x - 5$", "take $4x$ from both sides, the smaller $x$ term"] - ["$15 = 3x$", "add 5 to both sides: this undoes $- 5$"] - ["$x = 5$", "divide both sides by 3"] - ["Check: $4 \\times 5 + 10 = 30$ and $7 \\times 5 - 5 = 30$", "both bills are 30 dollars"] picks: - step: 4 q: "How do you undo the $- 5$ in $10 = 3x - 5$?" options: - "Add 5 to both sides" - "Take 5 from both sides" - "Add 5 to the right side only" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That makes it 5 = 3x - 10: the minus is still there. Use the inverse and add.", "Whatever you do to one side, do to the other."] answer: "5" tolerance: 0 answerLabel: "Gigabytes" feedback: - ["15", "That is $3x$. Divide by 3 to get $x$."] - ["3", "That is the number in front of $x$. Divide 15 by it."] criteria: - "I wrote the two bills and set them equal." - "I did the same to both sides on every line." - "I checked 5 gigabytes in both bills and got 30 dollars each." explain: "$4x + 10 = 7x - 5$ gives $15 = 3x$, so $x = 5$ gigabytes. Both bills are 30 dollars: for more than 5 GB, plan A is cheaper." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The prices are made up for the task, and real plans also have data limits and fees. Write the two bills, set them equal, solve one step per line, check in both bills, and type the number of gigabytes. **Also used in** - **Phone plans and hire deals.** Where two deals cost the same tells you which to pick for the amount you use. - **Routes and trips.** Two hire companies or two routes can be compared the same way: when are they equal? - **Next.** Inequalities say when one deal is cheaper, not just when they match. ```teacher summary: Students solve linear equations with x on both sides, brackets, negative answers and fractions by doing the same to both sides, writing one step per line, and verify every answer by substitution; a graph shows the solution as where the two sides meet (AC9M8A02, node 2). time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 15 min · Practise and Make 12 min struggle: "Signs: undoing a minus, and the x terms moving across. Ask for one step per line, and make the check in both sides a habit, not an extra." goals: - I can solve an equation with x on both sides, including negatives. - I can solve an equation with brackets by expanding first. - I can check my solution by substituting it into the first equation. before: > Do the working check yourself first. Students need The balance method (Year 7), Expanding brackets, and adding and multiplying negatives. This is a hinge node: inequalities (next) use the same moves, and sign slips carry over. The common mistake is undoing a term with its own sign (taking 7 away to undo − 7); it is planted in Ben's working and again in Practise. The working check marks each line against the one before, so students see the first step that went wrong; the last line must be x = … running: - "Predict: take a show of hands, then ask how students chose: trying values is fine, and leads to checking." - "Run: ask what P's y-coordinate means (the value of both sides)." - "Investigate: model the worked example, saying why the smaller x term moves (so x stays positive)." - "Modify: for the no-solution task, ask what the graph would look like." - "Make: collect students' equations and solve one together." - "Paper: the plans task is worked in books; the page marks the number of gigabytes (5) and the reason for adding 5. Books out, and look for the same thing done to both sides on every line." stuck: - see: A student takes 7 away to undo − 7 (Ben's mistake). ask: What undoes taking 7 away? fix: "Use the inverse: add 7 to both sides." - see: A student leaves x on both sides after the first step. ask: Which x term will you remove from both sides? fix: Take the smaller x term from both sides first. - see: A student expands only the first term of a bracket. ask: What does the number outside multiply? fix: "Every term inside: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6." stretch: "Solve (x + 4)/2 = (x − 1)/3. (Multiply both sides by 6: 3x + 12 = 2x − 2, x = −14.)" support: "Use the Run graph to check answers: drag P to the meeting point." leads: > Next: Inequalities (node 3), which solve the same way except when multiplying or dividing by a negative. Where it leads: simultaneous equations (Year 9 and 10), and rearranging formulas with the subject in two places. exit: q: Solve 4(x − 1) = 2x + 6 and check. a: "4x − 4 = 2x + 6, 2x = 10, x = 5. Check: 16 = 16." explain: > To solve an equation, **do the same to both sides** until $x$ is on its own: 1. Expand any brackets. 2. Take the smaller $x$ term from both sides, so $x$ is on one side only. 3. Undo the numbers with the inverse operation (add to undo $-$, subtract to undo $+$). 4. Divide (or multiply) to get $x$. $3x + 7 = 5x - 9 \to 7 = 2x - 9 \to 16 = 2x \to x = 8$. **Check**: $3(8) + 7 = 31$ and $5(8) - 9 = 31$. On a graph, $x = 8$ is where the two sides meet. ```

# Graph boards for "Solving harder equations". Each side of the equation is a line; they meet at the solution.

# region: run
widget: graph
x: -1, 10
y: -10, 45
grid: 1, 5
snap: 1, 1
plot: y = 3x + 7
plot: y = 5x - 9
point P: 2, 0, drag
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: -1, 10
y: -10, 45
grid: 1, 5
plot: y = 3x + 7
plot: y = 5x - 9
cross: 1, 2
# endregion

# region: make
widget: graph
x: -1, 6
y: -10, 20
grid: 1, 5
slider m: -3, 6, 0
slider c: -10, 15, 0
plot: y = 2x + 1
plot: y = mx + c
cross: 1, 2
# endregion
